controls.title: Define continuity and recovery requirements
controls.statement: Use business impact analysis to identify critical services, dependencies, minimum operating needs and achievable recovery time and recovery point objectives.
controls.risk: Recovery effort can restore the wrong systems in the wrong order while critical services remain unavailable if business priorities and dependencies are not defined in advance.
controls.scope: Critical services and their business processes, information, technology, facilities, people, suppliers and IT and OT dependencies.
controls.examine: Review business impact analyses, critical-service definitions, dependency maps, minimum operating requirements, recovery objectives and accountable approvals.
controls.interview: Ask business and recovery owners how they determine service priorities, tolerable disruption and dependencies across internal and third-party services.
controls.test: Sample critical services and trace approved recovery objectives to supporting systems, data, people, facilities and supplier arrangements.
controls.expected: Critical services have approved, achievable recovery objectives and complete dependency information that can guide restoration priorities.

mappings.basis: Requires business impact analysis to establish achievable recovery objectives aligned with business objectives.
Requires identification of essential functions, contingency requirements, recovery objectives, restoration priorities and metrics.
Requires recovery time and recovery point objectives for assets supporting the function to be included in continuity plans.
Requires continuity planning to minimise disruption to critical services and assets based on assessed risk.

controls.title: Maintain integrated continuity plans
controls.statement: Maintain coordinated plans for sustaining minimum operations and restoring services after cyber incidents and other significant disruptions.
controls.risk: Separate or incomplete plans can leave teams competing for resources, overlooking dependencies and extending disruption to essential services.
controls.scope: Continuity and recovery arrangements for critical and risk-significant services, assets and supporting external providers.
controls.examine: Inspect continuity plans, emergency and incident-plan integration, dependencies, roles, contacts, alternative arrangements, restoration sequences and review history.
controls.interview: Ask business, incident and recovery leaders how plans work together and how changes to services, suppliers and technology are reflected.
controls.test: Walk a disruption scenario across related plans and verify consistent priorities, handoffs, dependencies, resource assumptions and restoration actions.
controls.expected: Plans are current and mutually consistent, sustain defined minimum operations and provide workable restoration actions across key dependencies.

mappings.basis: Requires a maintained continuity plan that minimises the impact of significant disruptions on critical services and assets.
Requires plans for a broad range of emergencies to be integrated into the business continuity plan.
Requires continuity plans to address potential impacts from cyber security incidents.
Requires a maintained contingency plan addressing essential functions, recovery, responsibilities and eventual restoration.
Requires resilience plans and objectives to align and document internal, technical and external dependencies.
Requires restoration capability within the timeframes defined by continuity or incident-management plans.

controls.title: Exercise continuity plans and improve them
controls.statement: Test continuity plans against realistic high-priority disruptions, compare performance with recovery objectives and complete corrective actions.
controls.risk: Plans that have not been exercised may rely on unavailable people, systems or suppliers and fail to restore critical services within expected timeframes.
controls.scope: Continuity plans, recovery teams, critical services and the internal and external dependencies needed during disruption.
controls.examine: Review the exercise program, scenarios, participants, observed results, measured recovery performance, corrective actions, owners and completion evidence.
controls.interview: Ask business and recovery leaders how scenarios reflect material risks and how failed assumptions or missed objectives change plans and investment decisions.
controls.test: Sample exercises and trace significant observations through approved corrective actions to verified completion and updated continuity arrangements.
controls.expected: Exercises address priority risks, measure performance against objectives and produce verified improvements to plans, capability and dependencies.

mappings.basis: Requires contingency-plan testing, review of results and corrective action.
Requires periodic and trigger-based continuity-plan evaluations and exercises.
Requires continuity exercises to address higher-priority risks.
Requires test or activation results to be compared with recovery objectives and plans improved accordingly.
